span.p: Part 1 closing — K-Means / Hierarchical / DBSCAN, all HARD assignments

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

p.b: What if cluster membership is genuinely uncertain?
p.small: model it as a probability, not a label

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
§3 GMM · p(x) = Σₖ πₖ N(x; μₖ, Σₖ)
a universal density estimator · also a latent-variable model: z ~ Categorical(π), x | z=k ~ N(μₖ, Σₖ)
generation: sample z then x | z · discovery: given x, infer p(z|x) — the soft cluster

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
§4 fit θ by maximum likelihood · log p(X;θ) = Σᵢ log Σ_z p(xᵢ,z;θ)
log OF a sum — no closed form, intractable

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
§5–6 introduce q(z), decompose exactly · ln p(X;θ) = L(q,θ) + KL(q(z) ‖ p(z|x))
KL always ≥ 0 ⇒ L(q,θ) is always a lower bound (the ELBO)

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

p.small:
E-step: q(z) = p(z|x;θ) → KL → 0 → bound = true likelihood
M-step: maximise L(q,θ) over θ, q fixed → likelihood can't drop
'mountain-climbing': reshape the bound to touch the peak (E), then climb the bound (M)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

p.small:
E-step → γ(z_nk), the responsibility: soft P(point n ∈ cluster k)
M-step → μₖ, Σₖ, πₖ re-estimated as responsibility-weighted averages

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: §9 PLSA — the same derivation on discrete text (Gaussian → Multinomial; γ → per-word topic responsibility)
